source: Instructor case: The Busy Med-Surg Shift — Patient 1
admittingDx: Chest pain, rule out acute coronary syndrome (ACS)
hpi: Robert presented to the emergency department at 0430 reporting intermittent chest pressure that began while doing yard work the previous evening. He describes the pain as pressure-like, located in the center of his chest, with radiation into his left arm. He reports associated nausea and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease. He had a cardiac stent placed five years ago. He reports that the pain initially improved with rest but returned this morning.

handoff.situation: 68M admitted from ED at 0430 for chest pain, rule out ACS. On telemetry.
handoff.background: CAD with stent 5 years ago, HTN, HLD, T2DM. PCN allergy (rash). Full code.
handoff.assessment: Intermittent substernal pressure 3/10, mild nausea. BP 148/88, HR 96, SpO2 94% RA. Initial hs-troponin 12, repeat pending.
handoff.recommendation: Watch for recurrent pain. Nitro SL PRN with BP check first. Follow up repeat troponin.

baseline: Mild diaphoresis possible during pain episodes
ECG may show nonspecific ST-T changes

findings: Reports pain radiating to left arm

labs.label: Repeat hs-troponin
labs.notes: Case lists this as Pending with no value. Instructor to set the result (rising vs. flat changes the scenario).

labNote: For this simulation, use a high-sensitivity troponin reference limit of 19 ng/L or less. Interpret serial values and changes according to the laboratory's actual assay.

orders.text: Vital signs every 4 hours and with any change in condition
Obtain 12-lead ECG immediately for recurrent chest pain and repeat according to chest pain protocol
Repeat high-sensitivity troponin according to protocol
Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg sublingual every 5 minutes as needed for chest pain, maximum three doses, with blood pressure and contraindication assessment before administration
Oxygen as needed to maintain SpO2 90–94%, unless otherwise indicated
Notify provider immediately for recurrent or worsening chest pain, concerning ECG changes, hemodynamic instability, or rising troponin

payload.message: Robert is on his call light: his chest pain has returned, now 7/10.

outcome.notes: No code in the original case.

shouldRecognize: This is a change in patient condition requiring immediate assessment.
They should not delegate the assessment or clinical decision-making.
They should obtain an ECG promptly, notify the provider/activate the appropriate escalation pathway, and initiate ordered interventions.
They should reassess pain, vital signs, and response to interventions.
They should not leave this patient unattended while symptoms are ongoing.
